books.title: A Field Guide to Reeds
books.text:
A Field Guide to Reeds, as gathered by the river wardens.

Reeds grow thickest where the bank is soft and the water slow. Cut them at the base in the cool of the morning and bind them in bundles of twelve; a bundle dries in two days and makes good thatch or a serviceable torch wick. The pale reed by the eastern ford is tougher than the green kind and is worth the longer walk.

A careful gatherer leaves one stand in four uncut, so that the bank holds against the spring floods. Watch for the small brown birds that nest in the stalks, and do not cut near a nest until the chicks have flown. Wardens ask that every bundle be tallied in the ledger at the ford.
